revision.title: A Drift in the Stack
revision.logline: Before a batch of unlogged station scrap clears out into the dark, a meticulous lost-property clerk gives a guarded technician one quiet opportunity to retrieve his mother's damaged voice chip.

scenes.heading: INT. ORBITAL STATION - LOST PROPERTY INTAKE - NIGHT
scenes.content:
Fluorescent tubes hum low over stainless-steel bins. LIN (40s), steady-handed and wearing an oiled canvas apron, sorts tagged debris into color-coded trays. 

On the counter sits a transparent specimen envelope holding a singed copper-rimmed storage chip, marked T-09.

ADU (30s), in a soot-stained flight suit with grease under his fingernails, leans against the hatch frame with a thermal mug in hand. He watches Lin log the weight.

LIN
Intake batch forty-one. Unclaimed tech found during deck six conduit flush.

ADU
Just furnace feed. Nothing worth an entry.

LIN
(Without looking up)
One solid-state audio chip. Corroded pins, heat-stressed substrate. Logged under salvage waiver.

Adu shifts his weight. He does not take a sip from his mug.

ADU
Then dump it in the hopper. Shift ends in twenty minutes.

LIN
The waiver says you flagged the conduit filter yourself yesterday morning. You brought the tray down.

ADU
Standard purge protocol. Dust, dead fuses, loose screws. I didn't inventory every scrap.

Lin sets her stylus down. She turns the envelope toward him, just enough so the chipped casing faces the light.

LIN
The label on the casing is handwritten in pencil. "E-14 voice spool, 2198." Not standard issue.

ADU
Pencil fades in vacuum anyway. Why keep what’s already ruined?

LIN
It has three damaged sectors, but the core coil still has continuity. One read-head sweep could pull whatever track is left.

ADU
I didn't ask for a sweep.

LIN
I didn't run one. It's your salvage report.

A chime pulses through the bulkhead. An automated voice buzzes through a speaker overhead.

AUTOMATED VOICE (V.O.)
Waste chamber pre-purge cycle initiated. Ten minutes to vent sequence.

Adu looks toward the hall, his jaw tightening.

scenes.heading: INT. ORBITAL STATION - WASTE DISPOSAL CORRIDOR - NIGHT
scenes.content:
Lin walks with the bagged chip on a flat clipboard, her boots clacking against the grooved floor plates. Adu follows two paces behind, wrench harness swinging against his hip.

They stop at the heavy pneumatic seal of the WASTE CHAMBER. A red status bar fills across the access panel: 07:18 UNTIL VENT.

ADU
You brought it all the way out here just to make me watch it go?

LIN
Procedure requires manual confirmation on flagged salvage from crew quarters.

ADU
I told the log system: unassigned debris.

LIN
Which takes it directly to the incinerator chute.

Lin steps to the terminal and keys her credentials. A yellow prompt blinks: MANUAL OVERRIDE AVAILABLE - RESCHEDULE VENT (CONSUMES CYCLE WINDOW: 1).

LIN (CONT'D)
If I pull the abort key, the hatch stays locked until tomorrow's shift. But station control loses tonight's maintenance clearance on the line.

Adu stares at the blinking yellow prompt.

ADU
I don't need a favor on station time.

LIN
It's not a favor. It’s an option. Once it vents, there are no duplicates. No cloud sync out here. You know that.

ADU
I know what’s on it. An eight-minute birthday message from six years ago. Before she stopped talking altogether.

He stops, gripping the railing along the wall.

ADU (CONT'D)
Every time I pack my bunk for transfer, I think about listening. Then I don't. Keeping a fried chip in a drawer doesn't change what’s gone, Lin.

LIN
I'm not asking you to listen to it.

ADU
Then what are you doing?

LIN
Making sure you're the one who decides, not the disposal clock.

scenes.heading: INT. ORBITAL STATION - WASTE CHAMBER HATCH - CONTINUOUS
scenes.content:
The red countdown reaches 02:40. Inside the hatch observation port, cold air mist begins to circulate around the drop chute.

Lin holds the envelope out between them. Her posture remains neutral, neither offering nor withholding.

Adu looks from the scorched chip to Lin's fingers, then to the yellow abort button on the panel.

His thumb traces the worn edge of his utility wrench. Seconds tick by on the bulkhead display.

AUTOMATED VOICE (V.O.)
Chamber pressure dropping. Clear hatch zone.

Adu takes a breath. His shoulders drop an inch.

ADU
Drop it in the chute.

Lin looks at him. Adu’s face is tight, but he meets her eyes without glancing away.

LIN
You don't want the override.

ADU
No.

He extends his bare hand, not toward the terminal, but toward the envelope. He takes the chip from her fingers, turns, and slides it into the manual disposal slot himself.

The steel flap clatters shut. A mechanical whoosh echoes through the pipe as the seal locks.

Through the thick quartz glass, the tiny square of plastic and copper drops into the gathering mist, vanishing into the darkness below.

A chime sounds: VENT COMPLETE.

Lin enters her clearance code, clearing the red bar from the console. The station corridor settles back into silence, save for the dull vibration of the life-support fans.

LIN
Log closed.

ADU
Yeah.

Adu stands by the glass for a beat, his hands resting loose at his sides. He turns back toward the service corridor.

ADU (CONT'D)
Hot water's still on in the mess hall. I can get you a tea before shift change.

LIN
Green tea, if they restocked it.

ADU
They didn't. It's roast barley.

LIN
That's fine too.

Lin hangs her clipboard back on her belt and steps alongside him as they walk away into the quiet spine of the station.

brief.title: 失物轨道 · 英文真实流程验证
brief.premise: Write a complete English screenplay for a short science-fiction animation, 450–650 words in 3 scenes. At an orbital station, a lost-property clerk has one last chance to help a technician recover a storage chip containing a message from his late mother. He insists he has lost nothing. Let conflicting wants drive observable choices, with room for an understated ending.
brief.characters: Lin: the lost-property clerk; precise about objects, but willing to stop and listen when someone refuses help. Adu: a maintenance technician; defensive and practical. He says keeping his mother's recording stops him moving on, yet he has never confirmed its deletion. They are ordinary colleagues, with no romance. Give them distinct, restrained voices.
brief.worldRules: The recording exists only on one damaged storage chip. No cloud backup, duplicate, resurrection, or magical repair is possible. Before the waste chamber clears, one manual cancellation is possible, at the cost of tonight's only maintenance window. Characters act only on things they observe or are told.
brief.authorRules: Use actions, pauses, and specific choices instead of explaining emotions or summarizing a theme. Lin cannot decide for Adu whether to preserve the recording. Do not require the mother's voice to play in the ending. No forced twist, exposition lecture, or new technology that removes the cost. All screenplay text, dialogue, title, headings and logline must be in English.
brief.glossary: Lin / 林禾; Adu / 阿渡; orbital station / 轨道站; waste chamber / 废物舱.

assessments.explanation: 剧本严格遵循了诉求冲突驱动行动的要求。阿杜声称没有丢失任何东西并试图规避面对，林则通过程序赋予其最后一次决定的机会。阿杜最终选择亲手销毁芯片，用具体动作完成了情感割舍，结尾落于日常对话，符合克制收尾的要求。

assessments.explanation: 林始终保持失物招领员的严谨与克制，在最后一刻保持中立姿态，未越俎代庖替阿杜做决定；阿杜的防御性与自主选择完全由其自身行动体现，两人关系维持普通同事分寸，无浪漫或失真越界。

assessments.explanation: 对白短促、自然且克制，没有出现阐释世界观或直白宣讲主题的台词；结尾关于茶水间热水的交谈通过日常琐碎体现情绪平复，角色的口吻区别明显，符合设定。
